quote.l: „– Dans l’art dangereux de rimer et d’écrire,
Il n’est point de degrés du médiocre au pire.“

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My guardian – –

set.p: (The scene is a room with a central door and side doors.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Will he keep me waiting much longer?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: You know that my guardian – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Your faithful maid will certainly come.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: A touching sight! Since yesterday morning, when they last saw and kissed each other, the warmth of their hearts remains unchanged!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I’ll leave them alone to bill and coo. My pigeon is probably already waiting for me too. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Speak, queen of my heart!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: The separation that lies before us – –

set.p: (The scene is a richly furnished room.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Bliss of my life! (He rushes into her arms.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ah! Surely another letter from – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: The grief of love shall overwhelm us in excess – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My uncle wants to wed me to the country squire – –

sp.speaker: The Niece
sp.p: No, already two minutes past the appointed hour, and still he is not here! Hark! – „Do I not hear footsteps echo?” Isn’t there noise in the corridor? – No, it’s the little dog in the hall, who quails at Miez, the gray tomcat. – – Ah! I feel like a cloistered maiden walled up alive! – – He is still not coming. If I did not love him so exceedingly, I would give him a sound scolding for not being punctual – – But hush – Who goes there? Ha! My maid?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: My case is won, I have a fortune; so I see no reason – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Could you think me so frivolous, as to leave my maternal inheritance in my uncle’s hands, and with hasty step flee with you – –?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: A hasty wedding has ne’er been rued! So if it must be – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Would you make a jest of our plight?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: By marrying me to the son of his old friend, my uncle and guardian seeks to make me wretched.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: In any case, I am. You can count on me.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Whatever may come to pass: If you are mine, I defy a world full of adversities.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: I am already in love – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But the one I have chosen – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: He has won his lawsuit; therefore – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Is he here?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My future – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Dearest and best of Guardians – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But I have already given away my heart – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: What care I for the lawsuits of young fops! You know my conclusion, and with that – enough!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: He will be here shortly.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Nay, a foolish –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Little worm! Would you shine, and it is not yet Saint John’s Eve?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Have but a little patience with me yet, I implore you with the fervour of a child!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Though I am your ward, yet I am not your slave –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Dearest friend! Shall the tender bond of marriage ever unite me with him?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: A commonplace child from some fashionable novelette!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Miss, compose yourself!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: March! off to your chamber.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Could it be? Even imprisonment – –?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Who would despair!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Quickly, bring him in as well! We are unobserved. He must help us think this through. – – A troublesome matter for many a young gentleman!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: – That would compel you – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: How can you doubt? Had I not held him back, he would have flown at the old man’s throat. He is standing outside in the antechamber.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Is it true, then?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: According to my Guardian’s will – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Heavens! What a barbarian!

div.head: Ninth Scene.
div.stage: The Chambermaid. The Lover. The Servant.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Stratagem? „That is in my department!“ exclaims a famous writer of jest and stratagem-play.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Excellent! That has the metallic ring of genuine lover’s speech! (to the Chamberm.) Say then, my confederate, where shall we stitch our little piece of roguery?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Let us think no more on that! It might spoil our entire good humour—especially if that letter which arrived late last evening – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Here is my master, and here I am.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Confounded machinations of some match-making old man!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: How? But not by any stale, much-abused stage-device –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Out with it, sly dog! (To the Chamberm.) There’s no eavesdropper about, is there?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: What? A letter – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Strictly speaking, it is improper to disclose the plot of such a comedy beforehand; yet I am a genius, certain of my success, and so shrink not from publicity.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Hm! Dare I? Yes, I dare. Even were my conspiracy betrayed, even were it reported to the old man; even if he were wiser than, in a like case, the late Signor Doria of Genoa – still I retain my courage; as it were, a Fiesco in the republic of cunning servants. Nor will my master betray me, and to you (to the chambermaid, whom he attempts to kiss, though she either rebuffs him or, if she fancies, may allow it) — to you I press a seal upon your lips.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What? Do not think I shall stoop to one of those insipid stage-servants who achieve success by some exhausted stratagem – – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: You torture me when you do not speak more plainly.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Patience! Time will bring counsel. Here is a bringer of comfort.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So then, the name must remain secondary. They mean to make it hard for me. I am to carry out a most particular intrigue. Well! Two hundred ducats must be earned.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Know then, you my astonished confidants: the bridegroom is already here.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Yes. I am that unfortunate, foredoomed lover. (to the Chamberm.) Tell me then, what is his name?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So, we know not his name, we know not his character. In truth, we know nothing of him – so much the better! All the harder he is to portray; and thus all the easier for me. I shall create a character for him.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: My adored one!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Indeed, I am that pitiful soul, from whose very lips they would snatch away the bride – (to the Chamberm.) Does he not move thy pity? – Come, tell me quickly, what is his name?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I am dizzy!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Do you mean to mock us?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Arch-rogue!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Quick then! I’ll throw myself into the part. The old man knows me not, and if he does know me, yet he must not know me. That suffices me; and so he shall not know me!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: At last you draw near to this heart!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: You! You! Be not too forward!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Take heed, that you say not too much.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Agreed, you womanly Cartouche, you Black Fritz! But make haste, and bring me the fish even as you took it. In the hut by the pond I wait for you. –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: A notable instance of German fidelity! Yesterday they were together: today they begin afresh. A love such as one hardly finds, even upon the stage!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Do so. But quickly! You shall find me in the garden by the orangery.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Guard your tongue. I may take offence.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Now, do not be angry, dear sir. I was but imagining myself into the role of an ordinary comedy-servant, and – – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Then shall we go?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: What bliss, to be with you!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Could I live without you?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So go ahead, and act according to your former speeches. You are, after all, the soul here; I am but the body.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Hm! Very good! Almost fine, one might say, were it not entirely within the order of things. – Well then, forward, knavish servant!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: At your service. A modern servant, whom his master is compelled to employ in weighty matters, may be impudent enough to say everything to his master’s face; only, he must yield at the right moment, to show who is the servant and who the master.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Even if I truly be that; yet are all the virtues so united in me, that I must needs be modest, and –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Oh, oh! How my little heart flutters at this sight! Out to my darling; surely he is not far. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Indeed, sir. Already for the second time today I am here. You were not to be spoken with earlier.

Here is the letter. I rightly pilfered it away – – Now where is my sly fox? Ah! he’s already gone – His master with him. Quickly, after them – – Wait! Hark! The old man! He is speaking with someone. Away, swiftly, down the back stairs to my disguised one. (Exit.)

div.head: Twelfth Scene.
div.stage: The Uncle. The Lover. (Both enter at once.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But enough of tenderness! Let us now rather examine – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Permit me to tell you that you are half mistaken. I seek not your ward’s fortune, but solely the possession of my beloved, and thus I beg – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: In truth! My astonishment leaves me speechless to send her back. What do you want of me? Do you truly dare to inquire of me? Truly wish to speak with me, after I – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Why do you deny me my plea?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Tell me, what lies upon your heart –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My uncle’s plans for me – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Because I cannot abide you.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Vain hope, my romantic young sir! We are speaking of another sort of flight. Herr von ** shall take my ward, this tender dove, under his wings; for he comes –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What do you say?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: All Guardians, as per popular custom, are drawn from your comedies.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Your Grace would consume her goods and chattels alone. My niece shall now and never dip into the same dish with you.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Heavens! How shall we attain our goal?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: I heard of your renewed cruelty toward the pitiable girl. You are a tyrant!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: I simply do not wish you to be the husband of my ward.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: All that touches me not; I am consistent.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Free shall she emerge from the dungeon’s night, my beloved, whom you, like Elizabeth once did the Scottish Mary, do unlawfully imprison. Yet despite your obstinate temper, you will yourself be forced, when the fair one’s prison gate opens, to serve as jailer at her release!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: To a withered friendship of my uncle’s must I give fresh nourishment, by giving my hand in wedlock to the son of his old hunting companion.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Hoho! Miscalculated, Master Nürnberger. I still have the girl, and from my hands shall she receive the one who comes –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Well?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: There you hear it!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Well? Where is he then?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Prepare thyself to flee with me. No matter what our asylum be called, whether Kenilworth, or – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: I depart.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: A daring game I was forced to play. The old man I had to assure, he will, without doubt, suspect nothing now.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: This is no place for me to remain.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: To virtue, as to love, I am true; thus –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: In Heaven’s name!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Wherefore, since you are entirely superfluous here?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: As you please.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Would yet be but useless.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: True, I have lost the suit for my modest inheritance; but I can labour to sustain us – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Your most obedient servant!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: The one who was written for has arrived!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Bring him hither.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What means such speech? Am I not decent, not obliging, not agreeable, not welcome, not pleasing, not sufficient, not satisfactory, not pacifying, not rectifying enough for you?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: How now, my lord? What thoughts do you entertain of me? Do I seem otherwise to you than I do to myself? How were that possible? As I think of myself, so ought the whole world to think of me. Do I not appear to you charming, agreeable, delightful, beneficial, excellent, superb, enchanting, striking, venerable, amiable, perfect, inimitable – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Shall I, by marrying against my uncle’s will, run the risk of losing my not inconsiderable fortune?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Indeed, if – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Upon my honour! I know not myself – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Missed the mark! To that question I shall never reply.

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.p: Well then! What is your name?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: How? And yet I should be compelled to ask?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: In many a comedy the wards may flee with their lovers without their dowry. I do not do the one without the other; thus it is necessary – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Can such an important document lack the mention of my name? Therefore, to prevent substitution, confusion, and fraud, I must ask you: what is my name, my lord – – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: To the devil with it, your name is Baron von **

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: My dear Sir, a fool can ask more questions in a single breath than ten wise people can answer in an hour.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: All the thousand devils upon your accursed eloquence, and upon your yet more accursed presumptuousness! Well then, what is your name?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Quick! Quick! Do you want to be caught here? The master is coming through the corridor. Away! Out this way! (All exit.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: That I was bound to demand; for your own sake. I wish to see you, as soon as may be, upon one and the same intellectual level with myself. I abhor all spirit of caste. I love my fellow humans beyond measure, and I carry with me the great thought of reforming them all, wherever and in whatever they stand in need. With you I begin, by showing you how foolish it is to ask after things one already knows.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Errare humanum or humanum est. But better is better. Do not remain in error. Rather think upon the letter which my father wrote you.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Well, I think so; but – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Ah, the devil take it! You know as well as I do that you are the young Baron von ** –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: There we have it! So you do know. Why then did you wish to ask? Why indeed did you ask? And yet! If we consider it rightly, you should still have asked my name nonetheless.

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.stage: (alone; a folded letter in his hand.)
sp.p: „The oysters are here, the caviar is here, the pâté is here; thus – engagement!“ says the famous Kotzebue in the still more famous comedy: The Epigram; which is therefore the most famous of all epigrams, for no man’s ear has ever heard it. I say: the letter is here, I am here, and my niece is here, and the bridegroom Thaddäus Bocklümmel shall arrive, today or tomorrow. Thus: tomorrow is the engagement – and that is final! My Niece, this resisting and fondling with that Monsieur there, we are weary of it. – Ho there! Where is she hiding? (He rings. The Chambermaid enters.) Quickly! Fetch me your young lady.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: At once. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.stage: (stealthily draws forth a key and gives it to the Chambermaid, whispering something to her.)
sp.p: You shall be served presently, my good sir.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I understand. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Does it at last become clear that you asked without necessity? Or more precisely: that you asked nonetheless, because you had, in truth, to ask?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: What? What are you saying there?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: You go too far! Back down!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: There exists no opposition on the part of your Niece to my engagement with her?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: You summoned me, my Guardian – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So it is. Let us marry first and get to know each other afterward; for in me there is much, very much, exceedingly much, indescribably much, exceedingly much, unspeakably much, untamably much, enormously much to become acquainted with. I therefore doubt that you shall finish the task before our wedding; thus let us conclude the contract without further ado.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: I need not even find words. No is quickly said, and so I say: No, no, no!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: What? (secretly to her) You wayward girl!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: By no means! When I wish to hear something, I have enough in, by, from, with, and of myself to listen to.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Understand: My niece has no will whatsoever in this matter. Only my will is of consequence here; only this shall the notary incorporate into a properly worded contract and lay before you for signature.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Must? So – force? Very well! Might before right? Thereby you authorise me to commit against you the most flagrant injustice imaginable, and that I shall do. As soon as I have signed that accursed contract, I shall play you every prank that lies within my power. Your poultry yard, I know it, your pheasantry – at the inn they told me of it – is your Sans-Souci, your Mon-Repos. Just you wait! I’ll rally the sprightly youth of the village, and before ten minutes have passed, your pheasants shall be running about naked and the plucked hens shall raise such a clamour – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Exactly so, Miss Dreamface: the bridegroom is near at hand, and the moment he arrives, you shall be betrothed to him – prepare yourself accordingly.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Nothing further shall be necessary than to sign the contract; for since your heart is free, as the good Uncle says, you shall, without hesitation, choose me.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: You are a passionate smoker, that is town gossip. Very well! As soon as you place a pipe in your mouth, it shall be coated within with aloe and ipecacuanha; the tobacco I shall not poison, but I shall mix saltpetre into it.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Madman!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: I shall daub over your picture gallery in such a fashion that Rembrandt and Le Sueur shall look as though the chimney-sweep’s boy had wiped his nose and ears upon them.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Anxious concern drives me to you. One can hear the tumult in this house even from the street outside. Who is the stranger?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Lightning from clear skies! My Guardian, I implore you – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: But in mercy’s name! Hear me, I beg you!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: I will hear nothing, but from me you shall hear, shall this gentleman hear, shall all hear.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: You mean that in earnest?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: On my honour as a man!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: This instant, if you so will.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Good! But first let the word be kept.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: As spoken!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: With honour I proclaim – my work!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Mademoiselle Finicky is weeping, no less?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Then my beloved and I have long since exchanged our place of residence.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Bravo! Let the bridegroom from the country, and from Paris and London, see how he manages. We bring our little flock into the dry, so that our comedy finds its end; for that from my jest, once made public, any one of the countless famed playwrights of Germany will make a comedy is – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Indeed! A comedy. But what title shall it bear?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: No need for long pondering. It shall be called: The Uncle Who, Though Seeing, Is Blind.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: That were ungrateful of us; better we entitle it: No Barrier Resists Love.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Long titles also find admirers, so better still: As They Will, Not as He Wills.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Precisely, and: „From the English: „As You Like It;“ so that not every evening the playbill reads: „From the French.“

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My golden dream of wedded bliss –

div.head: Final Scene.
div.stage: The Lover. The Niece. The Chambermaid. The Servant.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Has there indeed a transformation befallen me?

sp.speaker: The Niece
sp.p: In vain I stare out into the dawn. I see him not coming. And yet he knows this is the best hour to whisper a word of intimacy with me. Ah! I am truly unhappy. To be sure, many a maiden has fared as I do: From a hundred and a hundred more comedies the same may be confirmed. But what avails it me? Though the spectators may have watched such plays nine hundred and ninety-nine times with delight: can that make me happy? Can that still the longing of my heart for my beloved? (Steps back from the window.) Who comes? Ha! Is it you?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: He draws nigh on the wings of love.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: The bridegroom’s affair, not mine.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Yes, from that side your little love-ship has poor wind; and it will have worse, once the letter which my Uncle late last evening – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My chosen one!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Upon thy breast vanishes every fearful foreboding.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: With thee, Heaven; without thee, Hell!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But I no longer belong to myself –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Let us sip but moderately from the chalice of love, and above all reflect – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Endless distress!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Another letter –?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Dearest maiden. (He embraces her.)

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Forget-me-not tales!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What should happen, then? Am I not independent?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Quickly! The old man is coming. Follow me. (All exit.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: How may I serve you, my Uncle?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No more delay! Your bridegroom is come, or will be anon; perchance this very day. Your engagement to him is settled. Therefore, make yourself ready to give him your Yes.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: So I am to part, then, from the sweet love of my – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: That does not happen so quickly.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: So truly you believe I should act irrationally were I to leave my not inconsiderable fortune in my Uncle’s hands, in order to – with you –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Would my love be pure, if it looked upon your dowry?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But my beloved – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Indeed, his lawsuit was lost to him; yet he has – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Who is a coward, who has neither wit nor discernment, and above all, no money.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: My hope – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Mademoiselle, do you take me for an uncle from a comedy in an almanac, with whom ward and lover may do as they please? Your chosen one is a – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: That is a matter for your irrevocably appointed husband.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Have I not spoken clearly enough, Miss Moonshine?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: With lawsuit lost or won, his love and my fidelity shall – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: You are murdering me!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: A girl –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No, a super-clever one –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Hoho! The bridegroom will bawl, hug, and kiss you into wakefulness –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Won or lost, lost or won: It is my procedure that is in question, and this commands you to obey, and that without any contradiction.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Do not suddenly ruin me. Grant me time, a small reprieve.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Bring him; we must take counsel (the servant exits) (alone.) The old man is away; Holland is in distress – Help! Rescue!

sp.speaker: The Niece
sp.p: My Guardian?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Only a little more time to reflect; I implore you!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Rescue! Rescue! O Love!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Cruel old man!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: That shall not go unrewarded.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Quite right! Such well-styled speeches one may hear a hundred times and still delight in them. (to the Chambermaid) Well then, my little sly one, how shall we set about it?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: In vain! All objections are at an end. I know by heart your litany on this subject. Heaven knows what famous authors they be, from whose more famous comedies you have learnt them.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Indeed, she is in bonds.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Be calm, Sir. There is but one remedy here, and it must be employed: it is called stratagem!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Quick, out with it! – But wait, are we being eavesdropped upon?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I have done the listening. The confounded bridegroom is announced, for tomorrow, for today –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Cruel fathers are dreadful; tyrannical uncles the most dreadful thing of all for youthful love. Rightly are they brought upon the stage in all their deformity, since life, real life, counts at least one specimen of such uncles, and that specimen is you!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Hm! »To be or not to be, that is the question!« – so once said some old Italian or Scotsman. Should I betray my plan? Would that not weaken the catastrophe? No matter! My applause is golden nonetheless.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Well then, one seeks the goal upon untrodden paths.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I burn with desire to see through your plan.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Exactly. Even if I carry out the plan entirely alone, there must first be understanding between the parties. The comedy is thereby extended by at least one scene, and such patch-scenes are the jewels in the golden circlet of excellent comedies. – So then, though I shall execute the affair alone, I will nonetheless confide it to you beforehand.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Is that meant to be wit, or defiance, or perhaps even both? Miss! Miss!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So then! The bridegroom of your beloved is no longer expected – he is already here!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Behold me, and you shall know what he looks like.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: More! More!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Sensible! Sensible!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: I must have been born for the stage, for I am to portray a man whom I know not at all, have never seen, whose name I do not even know, who, thus, in truth, is no man at all for me and cannot be.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: You are turning me into a corpse before my time.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Pst! That would be throwing out the child with the bathwater. Who here is to carry off the triumph of the stratagem? Answer: I! You shall have only the bride and with that you must be content.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Are you rambling?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Excellent!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Wait! Something comes to mind: the letter the uncle received yesterday, it might shed some light; be of aid.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Hoho! were we speaking of a cancelled ball. Girls all want to marry (sings) »Such is the course of the world« –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Then at least let me know – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Do not run off just yet. First take this earnest-money for faithful service beneath Cupid’s banner.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Then be swift. I shall costume myself in the meantime. The old man must not recognise me, though he knows me, and yet he shall have his joy or his anger because of me.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Then I am to count for nothing in your eyes, nothing but – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: You are, after all, a good soul! One cannot be angry with you. – So onward then!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Permit me, gracious Sir! (He draws a brush from his pocket, takes the hat from his hand, brushes it, and returns it with a courteous bow.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What is such an act called?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What would you mean by that?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: A fine model for a heroine of an almanac tale.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Then go, so that I may know where I am to go. Thus let the master follow the servant.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Certainly, sir. I wanted to speak with you an hour ago already; but you were not yet to be seen.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir, I have not yet shown myself, that is, not to you. You wish only to sing to me old, repugnant songs; variations whose theme is my niece and her money-bag.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: No. A subject fit to supply the saddest of romances – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Spare all your efforts. I belong to the unrelenting. Is that not known to you from comedies? Then do not wonder if I hold to my No.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No matter! You shall not have the girl.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Indeed I shall.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No, a disagreeable one, who wishes to annoy me.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Nevertheless! The moment she is free, she shall be gone, and I shall be gone with her.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Indeed? Then the hour she is free shall also be the moment of my wedding her.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Indeed? Was I so? Am I so? Youthful folly never lacks for epithets to bestow upon old age, when age dares prove itself wiser than youth would like!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: You see clearly, Sir, that your presence here is superfluous.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Who is to be forced against her own will – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.stage: (passing by the Lover, pushing him aside.)
sp.p: Out of the way, Sir.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Anticipate, prepare, so the old man may not grow suspicious.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I myself saw how he dismounted before the inn »Zur Maikatze«, exchanged a few words with the host, and then hurried here at full spur.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: To fall into a man’s arms, and remain therein until her final hour strikes.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What? Sir, what do you take me for? an ignoramus, a mocker, a persifleur, an obscurant, a pedant, a maleficant –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Sir, with me draws near your fortune. How do I strike you?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Here I am, sir, the one you signed for. How do I please you?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: A trifle, compared to what you may yet behold in me, once I let loose, once I position myself before you, depict myself, compose myself, expose myself, propose myself; once I make myself plain, declare, elucidate, unfold, pour forth, analyze, express, communicate, participate, decline and conjugate myself; when you shall truly know and name me, and be enflamed by me; when you shall behold me in proper light with your inner sight, comprehend – then shall you exalt me to the stars, in luminous distance: for you shall learn from me!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Alas! He is mad!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Horn of misfortune! If such a thing exists: it is poured out upon me.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Let only me be heard here! And to listen to me is child’s play, for I, the greatest philosopher of my age, have turned everything, yes the whole world itself, into a plaything. I am a card-sharp, a dice-thrower, a stage-player, an organ-grinder, player in love and in intrigue, a cabinet-gamer, a war-gamer. I play in village and city, in the scholar’s study, in the cowshed and in the ballroom, at the masquerade and in the dairy, in the magistrate’s court and the barber’s shop. I play with sculpture and gymnastics, with heraldry and metaphysics, with geometry and astrology, with skulls and with homeopathy, with nature and with the cure of hunger, with Rossini and Weber, with beefsteaks and goose-liver, with instruments and compliments, with opinions, apparitions, and negations – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir, do you wish to play a cursed game with me? Leave off these buffooneries.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: What? And yet you expect me to ask?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: In Heaven’s name! What then is your name?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Indeed; so that you may be made wise. I have studied pedagogy, you must know. By making people aware of their faults, the cruder, the better, one corrects them. You, however, have the fault of complete unawareness of yourself. Were it not so, you would not inquire after a matter which you ought long since to have known.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Off with you to your chamber, or I shall have a bridge built, like that once, now collapsed, bridge at Kenilworth, and whip you across it together with your lover.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: How can you doubt that my name must be known to you? Did you not receive a letter from my father, yesterday, the day before, or at least today?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Well yes; but – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir, how is it possible that I – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.p: Thunder and lightning! You are the young gentleman of ***.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: That would be the very devil!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Heaven! should he go too far, should Uncle suspect something. (She gives the Servant secret signals.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: What, Guardian mine? You would lay hands on my freedom, even my bodily freedom?

sp.speaker: The Servant
sp.p: But enough! More instruction another time. For now, let good manners prevail. I should like to be presented to your niece to see what impression I make upon her. Doubtless a wholly horrendous one – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: That would be the devil indeed!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: You! You! Be cautious!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: How come you to such a notion?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: But let us leave that. I burn with desire to see your young niece, to please her, to marry her – Lead me to her.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: March, I say! You shall be incarcerated. Clauren’s newest Forget-me-not I give you out of spite, your prayer-book out of mercy. (He leads her out.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Leave the notary aside when I am present. I am a jurist. Contracts I can draft myself, and thus we save the fees – but here, no contract is needed.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Indeed, Sir; for my niece must; your honoured father must; you must!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Heavens! the man is mad!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: And with a madman you would have me wed?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: To take no counsel, to consider nothing, to hear nothing, to alter nothing in one’s determinations; to persist, to stand firm, unbending, obstinate and iron-headed: that is what the spirit of the times demands of a youth of my nature.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Bah, neither the spirit of the times nor that other foolish thing, my niece there, shall be consulted: this very instant the notary shall be here.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: At your obedient service! Yes, I am your bridegroom. Let us be brief. Our pacts are in order. All that is lacking are the signatures.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.stage: (pokes her head first through the door, looks around, then steps in.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What must I hear? You make me into an outcast, a banished man, a despised, derided, displaced, disdained, annihilated being? Was it for this your honored uncle engaged me? Did he, with the most fatherly words, thus admonish you to receive me with love? Did he therefore invest your fortune at the most profitable interest, that it, along with your precious person, should escape me?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Oh come now, who would speak thus, Sir? My niece is merely confounded, but she will recover herself, reflect, find her speech again, and say to you – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Must? Must – a hard nut! Am I to crack it? Good! Then I shall give you yet harder nuts to crack. The very moment in which I must become engaged to this lady, I shall become your mortal adversary; your Mephistopheles, your Samiel. Nowhere shall I allow you peace. Every wish, every inclination, every hope, every joy, every day, every hour, every second shall I endeavour to wither for you. I shall vex, alarm, drive, hound, chase, torment, martyr you.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: But do you not see that the man is raving? Can you place your niece in such hands? Just hear my proposals! You recently expressed a wish for a riding horse from the princely stables: well then! I have succeeded in procuring one. Send tomorrow at earliest dawn to the suburb, to the Hôtel de Wibourg. Many strangers, noble guests, as you know, frequent the place. Among them is to be found an acquaintance, a friend for you: a grey steed – of finest breed – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Without delay, if you consent.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Adieu! But – parole d’honneur! (Exit.)

Verily! He locks her in. Ah, my poor young lady. – Hark! the old man grumbles upon the stair. He goes to the library – (speaking out the door) Quickly, come in. (The Servant enters.) Is your master with you?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir, what if I hold you to your word?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Do so.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: And you give me your word?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Here is my hand.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Is it possible that in this peaceful house such a murderous tumult can take place? Who here is in peril of life? Is it you, (to the Niece) my adored one? – Who is this gentleman?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Will you now finally shut your horrid mouth.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Nevermore! I shall cry out, roar against injustice, violence, atrocity, and betrayal!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Indeed. And the play might be called R. A. T. n., or: The Duped Old Man.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: R. A. T. n. — Really, All Trouble’s nothing.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Yes, yes! R. A. T. n. — Rowing Against Taste’s not proper.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Or better still: R. A. T. n. — Rambunctious Authors Tamed? never.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Who would speak so impertinently? R. A. T. n. — Ready At The nod, time to take our leave, that the curtain may fall and the pit kindly applaud.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Oh certainly. The imprisonment of his fair one has rendered him entirely perplexed.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Yes. He it is to whom I owe my happiness, who shall now receive the promised gold pieces and who may divert himself with his heart’s beloved wherever and however he pleases, while we two would undisturbed surrender to the bliss of love.

sp.speaker: The Servant
sp.p: We as well, darling?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Indeed. I intend to establish a boarding school for young ladies in the capital.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Yes, yes, it is you to whom I owe my life’s happiness, and your reward shall not fail. (to the Niece.) Let us go, that we may rejoice in our love undisturbed.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Call him in. (The Servant exits) (alone) Great counsel must be taken quickly. As yet we are undisturbed, and must strive for help. How goes it in Goethe’s opera? „Honor is pawned away, the crown and the palladium stolen!“

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Shall that concern us? We have the lead. None shall overtake us.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Quite right. As a comedy; but what title shall it bear?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Why, what else but: Love Victorious.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Indeed! But with the addition: by Love itself.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Or more pointed still: Love and the Servant’s Trick.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Only, let not all the honour at the end be heaped upon me alone. I might be called for to appear, and our players know so little of that, that most of them learn a speech of thanks by heart in advance.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ah! No matter how early I rose – my head is spinning – I am all confused – I would say stupid, were I not afraid someone might overhear. I do not want to read. The letters leap before my eyes, and – what is it Afanasja, or rather Athanasia, says? Yes: „Le coeur palpite!“ – Ah, my love! What is life, waking, sleeping, reading, or heart-throbbing without you? – – Ha! Do you come at last, my trusty confidante?

div.head: Ninth Scene.
div.stage: The Chambermaid. The Lover. The Servant.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Now, now, who would lose courage?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: From that, to be sure, little good can be expected. Who knows, moreover, what the letter contains, which he late last evening still – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Tell me, is my beloved coming?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ah, girl! Shall I ever press him to this bosom as my husband?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: There you have both master and servant. Fairly, you ought to be satisfied with the latter.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: But now let us take counsel – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Angel of my soul! (He flies into her arms.)

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Two lovers, who this very day are just as attuned as yesterday evening, when last they spoke and embraced.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: The Uncle! Quickly, follow me into the garden! (All exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: And the lock truly sprang shut behind her?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Everything is in order. Make yourself ready. The bridegroom is coming. The young gentleman von ** may perchance arrive this very day. The moment he arrives, your engagement to him shall take place.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: We would rather run away.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I hear the honoured master's cough. Quick, into the antechamber! (All exit.)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: What? You could seriously wish that I, fleeing with you, should forfeit the inheritance that my uncle holds in his hands?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: You are my everything, even without a dowry.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ah God, indeed! She is imprisoned.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: You shall hear it directly. I have long grown weary of your prattling. Tomorrow it comes to an end, perhaps even today. The young gentleman von **, your designated bridegroom, shall now appear. Make yourself ready to celebrate your engagement to him.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: You know that my uncle wishes to bargain me away, as it were, to the son of his friend.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Not so fast! Act in haste, repent at leisure – as old, I believe, as the ancient classics of which my cousin the superintendent makes such a fuss; so – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: The gracious master has left his chamber. Away, before he catches sight of you here! (All exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Turk of a guardian!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No questions from you! Obedience is all that is required of you. The young gentleman von **, the son of my friend, arrives today, tomorrow at the latest. You will then immediately give him your hand in engagement, and that is final!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Well then, my niece?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: What do I care about his lawsuit? I proceed: engagement – wedding!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: What? I should abandon my friend – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Easy! What must come to our aid in comedy when force accomplishes nothing? Stratagem!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Your bridegroom will see to that.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Be his lawsuit won or lost; in either case we have pledged ourselves to one another –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Should I tear apart the sweet bond of the heart that binds me to my beloved?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No, a foolish one – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Stratagem? I have that for sale! „Whoever bids the most, gets me!“ says one of the bandits in The Robbers; I believe the fellow's name is Schufterle.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: The moment the engagement hour strikes, you shall rise from the dead.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: – a pitiable one, rather –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: – A creature from a novel –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ugh, Uncle! You esteem me no more than – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Help, but think not of reward in doing so. Your master's generosity must not be provoked.

As I live and breathe, the lock snaps shut. What to do now? – Hark! the old house bear departs – the front door bell rings. He is gone. (Speaking out toward the door) Quick, come in! (to the servant, who enters) Where is your master? Is he here?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: – To abandon her moonlight love affair.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: We are here. What is to be done?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Fear not! Do you see this purse? It is yours, as soon as I – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Certainly not. The laborer is worthy of his wages. One hundred louis d'or if you assist me.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Yes indeed, she is locked up in her chamber. We have no castle dungeon, or she would be sitting in it.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What? Not perhaps like the tenant farmer Feldkümmel, of whom he may be a near relative? That would be nothing; such tricks are worn out.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Roguish knave. – – But we are not being overheard, are we?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: On such occasions, it absolutely tickles me to let my genius shine forth. – Come now, little maid! What is the enemy's position?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Matchmaker without equal!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What? You ask? Have more respect for my keen wit. You surely don't want me to be like Johann in The Sisters of Prague, or like valet Wind in Verlegenheit und List –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Behold him in my person.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: To the point!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Do not tease us so!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: The threatened fate breaks upon us at last; it comes and approaches in the form of a bridegroom, a promised one indeed, yet not the much-beloved bridegroom from Mexico; he comes tomorrow, perhaps even today – so the old man declared.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Very well then! Tremble, master! Quake, cowardly slave-girl! The dreaded bridegroom is already here.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: That matters not. I shall draw him out soon enough, and then you shall hear that his name is some Feldkümmel, or Bocklümmel, or Tippelskircher, or Hans von Birken, or Plumper, or some such ridiculous name.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Well then! What more?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Just don't be absurd.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Yes, who could answer that!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: O you uncle, full of obstinacy and marriage-making!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Excellent! That shall be my concern. I'll steal the letter away from the old man.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: I cannot allow that. You are not master now, that is to say, not in this matter. I predominate; I direct the battle; I stand at the helm.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: But come back soon. – I meanwhile will put myself into the clothes. With the costume, an experienced actor readily assumes the role he has to play. In the coat lies both the hero and the scarecrow. Quickly, to work on the old man!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Now? How do you manage that?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: How do we free my mistress? How do we drive away this toad of fate?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Understand me! Though you are now merely the instrument through which I shall let my plan ripen, I must not entirely avoid seeming to be your servant. In such cases, the theater has an excellent expedient. One first lets the servant speak foolishness to his master, and afterwards has him perform an action that makes clear the servant in him and the master in the other.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What do you mean by that?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Very well, then I must follow you, like a buck follows the bellwether that you would be.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So we go then – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What? Hopefully not on a path that other cunning servants have already taken before me.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So we go?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: You speak only half the truth. Indeed it is your niece's hand for which I repeatedly ask you.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: You really dare? You honor me with your visit? Me, who wants to know nothing of you? You really have – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Well then, we choose a brand-new means.

Perfect! Here is the letter. The old man had indeed left it lying with the newspaper on the sofa. Quickly – – but where are they? Already gone? So much the better! thus the clever fellow will be here for the comedy all the sooner. – Listen! the old man is making a racket outside. Quickly, before he notices me here. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir, I also do not wish to be seen, do not wish to be spoken to, at least not by you. What can you have to say to me? Only what I have already denied a hundred times; nothing else: for what else do you want than to marry my ward along with my ward's dowry?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Very succinctly spoken.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: That's just my way. Besides, my niece is locked up, consequently not at home for anyone.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Unfortunately I know that you act like a tyrant against the poor girl.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: That is what I strive for.
sp.l: The cleverest tricks I count among my own,
And what I'd be, I dare appear full-grown!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What if I tell you that I am not only, through my lawsuit, fully able to support a wife properly?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: And as soon as she is free, I shall run away with her.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: He comes!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Is he here?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: What? Can you doubt that it is the bridegroom?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Now? How so?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: From the inn »Zum grünen Esel« he hurries over to us, having just alighted from the country coach that still stands before the tavern.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: There is the young gentleman!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Bring him in, bring him in!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What do you mean by that? Do you take me for stupid, for ignorant, for silly, for impertinent, for unwise, for foolish, for presumptuous, for doltish, for idiotic, for senseless, for raging, for possessed, for – – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: God be with you!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Yes, yes, tell us – – We have no eavesdropper's ears to fear, do we?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: See in me your guardian angel, the bridegroom of your young lady niece. How do you like this bridegroom?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: The delight I feel over your final arrival is somewhat tempered by the astonishment with which – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.p: Devil take it, if you are your lord father's son, then you are called Lord von **.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So it is. Were you consistent with yourself, you would treat me differently. But because you perhaps think that people in the theater often sit where they should stand, and stand where they should sit, you want to make such a comedy fool of me, therefore you offer me no chair and don't even ask: »My lord, with whom do I have the honor?« –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: In a scene like this that we are playing, no one may eavesdrop, otherwise many a popular comedy would long since be no comedy anymore. – Therefore, tell us what you have in mind.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Not in the least.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: He's out of his mind! – Why should I have had to ask and then again not ask? Sir, you make me scatter-brained!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: There is no dissatisfaction on your niece's part with this marriage, is there?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: It would be a greater misfortune for you than for me if your young lady niece said no.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: You want to lead me onto thin ice like the lying Guildenstern did Hamlet; I should confess to you; I should tell you from the lowest note to the highest: that I should do. Do you think I am easier to play than a bagpipe? Nevertheless I will do it, will say it; for my genius knows no obstacles.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: What, Miss? What do I hear? You reject my hand? You despise me? You cast me off? You hurl me from you? You renounce me? You want to know, hear, see, perceive, learn, receive, retain nothing of me and keep it until you – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: My God, the man argues dreadfully! Do let my niece come to words, to think – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: You hear it yourself. She will not marry me – Good! So I will not have her either, absolutely not, completely not, utterly not, by no means not.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: So listen! Take advice!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: No! There is no way out. The man is truly mad.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: And yet you wish to give him to me as a husband?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: You speak into it too!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: You break my heart. What do I say? You have already broken it. My lip stammers, my tongue grows rigid, my fevers tremble, my pulse stops, my nerves twitch at the death-word you speak.
sp.l: That such grief should befall me?
O, dear maiden, let me say – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: There you have it. Who would burst in so bluntly? My niece will, if you give her time, find better words, and – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Braggart!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Fop!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Heaven! Is some misfortune occurring here? What does this gentleman want? Who is he?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Madman!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: From your chess machine that plays by itself, I shall remove the brass soul, so that with the wooden corpse you shall know nothing, absolutely nothing more to do than to stick it in the fire.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sir! You murder me..

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: That is what I intend to do, metaphorically speaking.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Forgive me for intruding once more. But I thought, had to think, that a precious life was in danger here; such tumult as – – This gentleman here? What does he want? Who is he?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Have you escaped from the madhouse?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Not at all! But in your house things shall go on as in a madhouse, as long as I remain in it.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So compose yourself then, my gracious lord – You, hold fast to the chair back to resist the fainting. Your beloved's bridegroom, that disturber, that dark spirit who would pass through our house – is already here.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What does that concern us. We travel far – far!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Without anyone learning where.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Through his stratagem we are united. Nothing separates us anymore. (To the Servant, throwing him his purse) Take your well-earned reward!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ah, my friend! When will he become mine?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Fresh courage, fair young lady!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: I truly feel unwell.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Fellow! do not lie.

sp.speaker: The Niece
sp.stage: (her head supported, at the table, alone)
sp.p: Flow, my tears, flow! What is a young maiden worth nowadays who does not daily weep her portion before she has spoken with the beloved of her heart? – But no! Weeping is harmful to the eyes. It causes the lashes to fall out. I will not be sad at the expense of my pretty face. Let him stay away as long as he will, the lingerer. – But wait! Someone comes. Now, is it you?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ah yes! From there it storms. Who knows what new thunderbolt lies in the letter that your guardian received late yesterday evening!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: My dear girl!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: In your arms I forget myself.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Divine bliss at your breast!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Here he stands.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Now to the more important matter. We must consider – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Let another endure that. I go to bring my sweetheart a morning greeting. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Fate! What is to become of us?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: I abduct you.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: You would be it?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So I thought.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Well, Uncle, here I am. And –?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Get away from me with such exclamations. I'm not moved by such novel-like babble!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: – Without leaving me the slightest hope of deliverance; unless it be through death –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Quick! Ask him to come in. (The Servant exits again) (alone) The house bear has withdrawn to his corner; the stage is empty and only this clever servant can fill it again. He must help. My young lady must be saved.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Indeed I am. I am that pitiable wretch from whom the bride is to be snatched, though he perhaps cares nothing for her. (to Chamberm.) So »weep not, weep not, my Cordelia.« – Tell me rather, what is his name?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Stratagem? That is my trade.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So it is certain?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Deploy your troops. The reward will not escape you.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Hear what I overheard. It stands in the letter. The old man finally has the bridegroom come; tomorrow – today already –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Yes, who would know that!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Done! Choose what no one has chosen.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Not a soul is near. (to Servant) Fire off your sharp-loaded thunder-gun.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Rogue!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Clever fellow!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: What?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Already?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: No matter. As if one could not guess what he is called! His name will be Plumper, or Theophilus Feldkümmel, or Thaddäus Bocklümmel, or Sebastian Lämmerzahn, or Hans von Birken, or whatever the honest Pomeranians in comedies are otherwise called.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Yes, I am that unfortunate one who is to lose the promised bride before he has even seen her. Weep a tear for his fate! – Speak, what is his name?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: If the answer to this question is to become the cornerstone of your clever edifice, then I pity you. The name is a secret.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: The admiration I shall arouse will be enormous. I know not the man; I know not what he is called, I have never seen him; nevertheless I will represent him.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Indeed, indeed! I see to it that I steal him away from the old grumpy tomcat.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Speak further!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Do not jest when need presses us.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Hold, little one! Take this trifle in advance first.

sp.speaker: The Servant
sp.p: What you do, do quickly. – The old man has never seen me, so quick into the clothes and to work.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Now, now! Just not too forward.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: How would it be if we could cast a glance into the letter that the uncle received?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: So his name is unknown? His character, his person as well? Tant mieux, so I represent him impromptu.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: And such action would consist – in what?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Forward then! According to your phrases, I am the servant, you the predominant one.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Buffoonery without end! March! Forward!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: What kind of action then?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Something occurs to me. How would it be? The letter that the uncle received – if we could read that: it might perhaps – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Well, forward with you, that I may give you as my guiding star the due respect – –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Mit Ihrer gütigen Erlaubniß! (Er läßt sich hinter ihm auf ein Knie nieder, um etwas an der Fußbekleidung seines Herrn zu ordnen, steht auf, tritt einen Schritt zurück, verbeugt sich und spricht.) So ist’s in Ordnung.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Bitten Sie, so viel Sie wollen. Unnütze Dinge zu treiben, ist heutiger Jugend Lieblingsbeschäftigung.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Mit nichten, mein Herr. Die Nichte nur begehr’ ich, nicht das Vermögen; drum komm’ ich, Sie nochmals zu bitten – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ganz recht. Der Brief kann uns nützlich werden. Ich will suchen, ihn zu erwischen.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: In der That, mein Herr; ich weiß nicht, was ich von Ihnen denken soll. Sind Sie von Sinnen? Sie fragen nach mir? Nach mir, der ich Ihnen längst erklärte, daß wir geschiedene Leute wären.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Wie? Sie verwerfen mich, ohne mir das Warum deshalb zu sagen?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Wird sich nicht thun lassen. Ein Anderer Halt-sie-vest ist bestellt, und der wird kommen; ja, ja, mein Herr, kommen!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Wie?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Darnach haben Sie nicht zu fragen.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Stiehl mit Glück und dann komm mir nach, neben an, zu der alten Suse; dort wart’ ich auf Dich, während ich mich costümire.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Allerdings; ich werde sogar mich selbst dazu zwingen, allein keine Minute eher, als es Zeit dazu ist.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Recht so! Titel, welche die leidige Mode unserer romanhaften, wahrhaftig nicht romantischen Zeit allen vernünftigen Vätern und Pflegevätern giebt, die der jugendlichen Thorheit Zaum und Gebiß anlegen wollen.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Was schiert das mich? Ich bleibe bei meinem Entschlusse.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Bei’m schwarzen Bock hielt ein Karrenwagen. Ein junger Herr stieg aus, sprach mit dem Wirthe und steuerte gerade auf’s Haus los. Da kommt er (am Fenster).

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So eile doch nicht so! Nimm erst dieß auf Abschlag meines Dankes (ihr Geld gebend).

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Den Alten sicher zu machen. Er ertappte mich ja mit meinem Diener – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Mein Herr, Sie finden hier keine Heimath –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Nun, junger Herr, was sagen wir nun?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Wohlan! Wo ist denn der Neuangekommene?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Das ist noch Nichts! Sie müssen mich hören! singen, räsonniren, declamiren, philosophiren, parodiren, haranguiren, extemporiren, improvisiren; sie müssen mich sehen! fechten, reiten, schießen, jagen, fischen, tanzen, würfeln, boxen, scharmiren, anatomiren, ballotiren, copiren, escamotiren, alligiren, amalgamiren, renoviren, restauriren, chiffoniren –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Herr, Sie ruiniren mein Gehör – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Recht so!

div.head: Fourteenth Scene.
div.stage: The former. The Servant (à l’incroyable gekleidet. Je auffallender, je besser! – Da die meisten unserer Volksschauspieler geborene Menschendarsteller sind, so würde es abgeschmackte Eitelkeit verrathen, wenn der Autor hier mehr als einen kleinen Fingerzeig gäbe.)

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Gott zum Gruß, mein Ersehnter!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Wer spricht hier, wenn ich rede? Ich, der Dialectiker und Eklectiker? der Pädagog und Demagog? Der Jurist und der Sublimist oder Sublimatist? Ich, der ich in Russland die Lebensgeschichte eines Kaviars und in Berlin einen Taschenalmanach über die sämmtlichen Folianten Deutschlands schrieb? Ich, der ich classisch schreibe wie Clauren, und doch nicht Verfasser des Mannes im Monde bin? Ich der ich besser dichte als Goethe, weil ich noch mehr schreibe als Gustav Schilling? Ich, der ich declamire wie Talma und der deutsche Schuster und agire wie Kean, Macready und die Statisten auf dem Hamburger Theater? Ich der ich commandire wie weiland Rinaldo Rinaldini und excerpire wie die Verfasser von Krünitzens Encyklopädie? Ich, der ich – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Herr, Ihre entsetzliche Gelehrsamkeit könnte mich eseldumm machen. Schweigen Sie –

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Was wollen Sie? Was meynen Sie? Was denken Sie? Was vermuthen Sie? Was ahnden Sie? Was hoffen Sie? Was erwarten Sie? Was wünschen Sie? Was begehren Sie? Was verlangen Sie? Was entdecken Sie? Was bezwecken Sie? Sie haben mich hieher verschrieben – ich bin da, nach Ihrem Willen; drum gilt jetzt auch mein Wille. Auf Ihren Antrieb werden Sie jetzt von mir angetrieben, aufgetrieben, fortgetrieben, ausgetrieben, in die Enge getrieben –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Alle Wetter! drei Schritt vom Leibe geblieben!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Drei Schritte vom Leibe!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Wie, mein Herr?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Nun, zum Wetter! Sie sind ja der junge Herr von **.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Aber ohne Verzug! – Ich habe eine brennende Begier den Alten zu bearbeiten. Zwar hat er mich ein Paar Male gesehen; aber das thut nichts. Das ist eben das Pikante bei dergleichen Verkleidungen, wie ich eine vorhabe.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Und doch machten Sie mir so eben diese Frage zur Pflicht?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sterben will ich, wenn ich darauf zu antworten weiß.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Eben darum. Muß in einem so wichtigen Briefe nicht von mir, nicht von meinem Namen die Rede seyn? Wer hat also hier nach meinem Namen zu fragen? Ich, mein Herr, nicht Sie! Um Sie zu prüfen, ob ich Ihnen der Rechte bin, muß ich fragen: Mein Herr, wie heiß’ ich?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Wahrhaftig, ich werde irre an Ihnen – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Sage nur, wie Du’s eigentlich anstellen willst.

div.head: Fifteenth Scene.
div.stage: Der Oheim. The Servant. The Niece. The Chambermaid.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Meine Nichte. – Der junge Herr von **.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Ihre Nichte wird doch nichts gegen eine Verbindung mit mir haben?

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Ei, warum nicht gar!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Geh nicht zu weit! Er mögte Etwas merken –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Herr, wollen Sie mich ganz confus machen? Fragen, und doch nicht fragen – nicht fragen und doch fragen?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Wie heißt die Redensart in vielen Comödien? „Folgen Sie mir, daß ich Ihnen unterwegs meinen Plan mittheile.“ Da fügt sich’s denn, daß der Herr dem Diener nachgeht.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sogleich soll meine Nichte hier seyn. (Heimlich zum Kammerm.) Geschwind! Ich habe Sie eingeschlossen. Hier ist der Schlüssel; hole sie!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ich gehe. (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Richtig, so heiß’ ich. Sie wissen’s also und fragten doch? Wieder richtig, denn es ist richtig, daß Sie doch gefragt haben, weil es richtig ist, daß sie eigentlich haben fragen müssen.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Da hören Sie’s! Sie will mich nicht. So will ich sie auch nicht. Ich stoße meines Vaters Willen um, ich stoße Ihren Willen um, ich setze meinen bisherigen Willen hinten an und nehme einen neuen Willen an, der da spricht: Ich will die Mamsell nicht!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Sind Sie von Sinnen, Herr?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Nein; aber ich will Sie von Sinnen bringen. Ich gebe Sie an als einen Carbonaro, zu deutsch Kohlenbrenner, als einen Häuptling irgend einer entsetzlichen Verschwörung, die Sie erst anzetteln wollen, und geht’s gut, so habe ich Sie nach kurzer Frist in die Bleikammern von Venedig gebracht. Mögen Sie’s dann machen, wie Casanova – wahrheitsliebenden Andenkens – ich will Sie nicht daran hindern, aber unters Blei sollen und müssen Sie –.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Spitzbube!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Nie werd’ ich Ihre Gattinn! Nie!

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.p: Ich rathe Dir es, zieh’ andere Saiten auf, oder – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Ich habe nichts mehr zu sagen. Mein Nein war deutlich genug ausgesprochen.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Abgeschmackte Romanennärrinn!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Bon! Sie thun das Aeußerste, das Gewaltigste, das Unerhörteste, das Incroyabelste an mir? Bon! So thue ich nun das Unerhörteste, das Gewaltigste, das Aeußerste, das Incroyabelste an Ihnen. Sie wollen mich nicht? Gut! So will ich Sie auch nicht – Taille faite!

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Lassen Sie Ihre incroyable Taille aus dem Spiele und nehmen Sie Raison an; lassen Sie sich rathen; hören Sie!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Heute noch, wenn Sie es erlauben.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Gott befohlen! Nur Wort gehalten – und, glückliche Reise! (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Nur gnädig, mein Gebieter. In der Regel muß der Liebhaber in der Comödie dem verschmitzten Diener, der ihm aus der Klemme helfen soll, Etwas zu Gute halten.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Ist das Ihr Ernst?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Mein völliger. Sie unterzeichnen also den Heirathscontract mir zu Gunsten?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Und mit solchem Unsinnigen können Sie sich einlassen? Geben Sie ihm doch den Laufpaß, ehe er Sie, Ihre Nichte, mich, uns Alle mit seiner Raserei ansteckt. Das Gütchen Walldorf, mein einziges Erbtheil – es hat Ihnen stets gefallen: wohlan! Ich überlasse es Ihnen für einen Spottpreis, für das Vermögen Ihrer Nichte. Geben Sie mir Ihre Mündel mit dem ihr gehörenden Capitale und Walldorf ist Ihr Eigenthum.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Noch ehe es dunkel wird.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Und Ihr Versprechen?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Geht pünktlich in Erfüllung.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Adieu. Glückliche Reise! (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: O weh! Sie bringen mich um.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Das will ich auch! Denn Sie haben mich ermorden wollen, indem Sie meinen Willen, das Höchste im Menschen, schmählich angetastet haben. Was ist der Mensch, wenn sein Wille nicht mehr frei ist? Nichts! Sie haben mich also zu Nichts machen wollen; darum will ich Sie zur Leiche machen.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Wir entfernen uns also?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Eine Frage, die zur Unzeit kommt, weil sie nur mir hier ansteht. Nur ich habe hier zu fragen: Wer sind Sie? was wollen Sie? was beabsichtigen Sie? was bezwecken Sie? was begehren Sie? was fordern Sie? was heischen Sie? was verlangen Sie? worauf trotzen Sie? worauf pochen Sie?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Dann mag der Herr Bräutigam noch ein Lustspiel nach meinem Lustspiele spielen; denn daß mein heutiger Schwank auf die Bühne kommt, ist gewiß. Er ist genau so interessant, als wär’ er aus dem Französischen übersetzt.

div.head: Final Scene.
div.stage: The Lover. The Niece. The Servant. The Chambermaid.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Aber sage mir, ist ein Wunder geschehen?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Mit Verlaub! Wir haben Vorsicht zu gebrauchen gegen den rechten Bräutigam. Er soll ja morgen eintreffen.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Wenn’s Ihnen gefällig ist, sogleich.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Allerliebst! Mag dann der rechte Herr Bräutigam vor leeren Schalen sich zu Tische setzen, wie Banquo’s Geist im Trauerspiele. Wir tunken in die süßgewürzte Schüssel der Liebe, damit aus dem heutigen Hokus Pokus ein Lustspiel werde.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Und Du? Willst Du’s mit mir wagen?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Zwar ist’s gefährlich; jedoch – wagen gewinnt!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: So geh denn voran, Du, der Du die verkehrte Welt mit mir spielst, indem Du mich zum Knechte machst und Dich den Herrn nennst.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ich bin’s. Wohl ist’s an mir, jetzt aufzutreten.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Treue Seele! Wird sein Kommen mir Versichrung, daß ich ihn einst ganz besitzen werde?

sp.speaker: The Niece
sp.p: „Es seufzt’ einmal um Mitternacht –“ Ei was! (das Blatt wegwerfend) Das paßt ja gar nicht auf meinen Zustand. Es ist jetzt heller Tag und ich seufze – muß seufzen; ach! Sollt’ er treulos geworden seyn? Seit gestern sah’ ich ihn nicht, und die Stunde des Wiedersehens hat doch schon geschlagen! Aber er kommt nicht – – Bist Du es, getreue Aja?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Das wäre ich freilich: jedoch alle dehors muß man nicht verletzen.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Ich lasse sie allein. Wahrscheinlich steht mein Schatz auch schon auf der Lauer.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Noch ringe ich mit Zweifeln.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Wieder ein Brief?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Halt ich Dich endlich wieder in meinen Armen?

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Was soll das heißen?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Lass’ uns haushälterisch mit unserer Zärtlichkeit seyn. Bedenke mein Theurer – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: O, daß ich Dich immer so umschlungen halten könnte!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Herr Vormund, Sie befehlen –?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Schäme Dich solcher Rede!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Gehorsamer Diener! Mag ein pfiffiger Bedienter in oder außer der Comödie noch so ungeschliffen gegen seinen Herrn seyn; kein Herr, folglich auch kein Publikum darf’s ihm übel nehmen; sobald er nur zu rechter Zeit, auf dem Theater, etwa kurz vor seinem Abgehn, einlenkt, und irgend eine Handlung begeht, die ihn ersichtlich von seinem Herrn geziemend unterscheidet.

sp.speaker: The Uncle
sp.stage: (tritt ein, die Hände auf dem Rücken, auf und ab.)
sp.p: Keine Minute mehr sollt’ ich der Närrinn Bedenkzeit geben. Kann Frau werden und ziert sich. Und wessen Frau? wessen Schwiegertochter? Die Frau des vortrefflichen Hans von Birken, der sich in allen Wissenschaften, so wie auch im Landbau und Gott weiß worin sonst noch, umgesehen hat; der der Sohn eines ehrlichen Deutschen ist, dem ich mein Wort gegeben habe. – – Also, keine Geduld mehr! (Einen Brief hervorziehend) Nach diesem Briefe keine Geduld mehr! keine! (klingelt. Das Kammerm. tritt ein) Meine Mündel, das Fräulein! Sogleich! (Das Kammerm. ab.) Warten Sie, Mamsell, hier gilt’s kein Maulspitzen, hier muß gepfiffen seyn.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Zu leben haben wir, also – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Sie haben mich rufen lassen, Herr Onkel?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Mein – unser Unglück ist gewiß, wenn meine Heirath mit dem Sohne des alten Freundes meines Vaters wirklich vollzogen werden soll.

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Und welche Handlung, zum Beispiel.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Der ein Sausewind ist – ein Johann ohne Land – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Mein Herz ist aber schon verschenkt.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Nun, zärtliche Daphne?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Sie verlangen, daß ich mich opfern, meinem Geliebten entsagen soll?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Sie heißt: stummes Spiel. (Er ordnet mit vieler Ceremonie Etwas an der Kleidung seines Herrn, tritt dann zurück und verbeugt sich, als wolle er sagen: „Ich bin fertig.“)

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Erfahren Sie, daß der Prozeß meines Geliebten – –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Geben Sie mir keine Frist?

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Sie bringen mich um’s Leben.

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Herr Vormund, Sie mißbrauchen Ihre Gewalt über mich!

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Ei, ei! Du hast Deinen Character ja gut studiert; fast zu gut für einen gewöhnlichen Intriguenspieler in den Comödien: denn die haben selten Character. Nun – voran!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Immerhin, wenn es Ihnen Vergnügen macht; jedoch zugleich bin ich auch ein bejammernswerthes – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Hüte Dich, wenn ich erst Gewalt – –

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Nein, nein, nein! ein widerspenstiges –

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: Herr Onkel?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Er steht vor der Thür.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: Fort, in’s Carcer! sagte mein hochseliger Rector, wenn ich ihm weißnasig über den Schnabel gefahren war. Fort, auch in’s Carcer mit Dir! Eingesperrte Vögel – zahme Vögel! Marsch!

sp.speaker: The Niece.
sp.p: – das sie in’s Verderben bringen wollen.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Herein mit ihm, und Du komm’ auch wieder. Man braucht Dich, man braucht mich – (der Diener ab) (allein.) Ach! was braucht der Mensch nicht Alles! Wir brauchen Entwicklung, denn die Verwicklung hat hier schon tüchtig überhand genommen.

sp.speaker: The Uncle.
sp.p: – Sich einem Manne hinzugeben. Wie viele tausend Mädchen haben das schon gethan!

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Herr, der Ihrige mit Leib und Seele! (zu dem Kammerm.) Sprich, Du Orakel uns’rer List. Was ist zu thun?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: List? Das ist Wasser auf meine Mühle.

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Da sind wir.

Wenn ich so fortfahre, werde ich der Kammermädchen vorzüglichstes; würdig daß ein Dichter eigends für mich ein Almanachslustspiel schreibt, um mich unsterblich zu machen. Kaum wird’s nöthig, einen Brief zu stehlen – husch! hab’ ich ihn weg. Wie ich es gemacht habe, das ist nicht nöthig anzugeben: Genug, ich habe ihn gestohlen und – da ist er! Fort damit an den Ort seiner Bestimmung! (Exit.)

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Gewiß nicht! Ein mattherziger Liebhaber, der in solchem Falle ein Paar hundert Dukätchen springen zu lassen scheuet!

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Nur nicht getobt! Damit wird uns nicht geholfen. List allein – –

sp.speaker: The Lover.
sp.p: Also wirklich gefangen die Königinn meines Herzens?

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Nicht doch! nicht doch! (zum Diener) Sage nur, sprich nur – –

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: Wie entledigen wir uns des Kommenden?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
sp.p: Das werd’ ich. Ein Genie, wie ich bin, wandelt eigene Wege.

sp.speaker: The Chamberm.
sp.p: So sag’ endlich, wie willst Du’s anfangen?

sp.speaker: The Servant.
